A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ContextMATH study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content across relocated statements and renumbered displays.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original evaluations of 61 models, formulation and error analyses, and supervised fine-tuning experiments, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the original benchmark evaluations, formulation analyses, and training experiments, including their detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: The SG/CS construction pipeline, generation and verification prompts, end-to-end fine-tuning, and dedicated formulation-model procedures remain unchanged. Appendix renumbering does not introduce a method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use AIME 2024/2025, filtered MATH-500, DeepMath training data, and AMC23/Math-Perturb transfer evaluations. The added discussion of GSM8K concerns prior work, not an additional evaluation.

E2.justification: The same 46 open-source and 15 proprietary models participate in the benchmark comparisons. The training-regime and formulation-stage comparators also remain identical; Cheng et al. is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Dataset filtering, accuracy metrics, model configurations, 50k/100k training regimes, decoding settings, and training budgets are retained. The evaluation details move from Appendix A.3 to A.2 without substantive changes.

E4.justification: Both retain the alternative-scenario consistency check, error classification, formulation necessity/sufficiency analysis, training comparisons, Math-Perturb robustness evaluation, and DeepSeek-R1 geometry case study. The new literature comparison adds no analysis experiment.

E5.justification: Both retain 16-sample open-source evaluations, single-pass proprietary benchmark evaluations, and the 16-sample formulation evaluation with the same seed-set statement. Statistical and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 have identical results. v1 Figure 4 matches v3 Table 5, and v1 appendix Tables 5–6 match v3 Tables 6–7. The plotted trends and qualitative case-study findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The conditional-probability definitions of formulation necessity and sufficiency in Equations 1–2 remain identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about ContextMATH, contextual performance drops, complementary formulation/reasoning bottlenecks, and the benefits and limitations of the training approaches.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly contrasts its formulation-bottleneck finding with Cheng et al. (2025), distinguishing simpler GSM8K problems from complex contextual narratives. This adds a substantive contextual interpretation; existing interpretations and qualifications otherwise remain.

D1.justification: Construction prompts, model/API details, inference settings, and the training recipe remain unchanged, including four A100 80GB GPUs and 1,200 optimization steps. The benchmark-release promise is retained; relocating the reproducibility statement does not change access information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Cheng et al. (2025) on abstract formulation and arithmetic computation, with a brief comparison in Section 4.1. The remaining related-work discussion and cited-work coverage are retained.

P1.justification: v3 moves the ethics and reproducibility statements into the appendix, makes the LLM-use statement unnumbered, updates cross-references, and adds contact emails and an acknowledgement. Apart from the short literature comparison, the main narrative remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1's logo changes from CORE-MATH to ContextMATH. The formulation-results display is relabeled from Figure 4 to Table 5, and appendix tables and boxed content reflow across pages. These are limited presentation changes to existing content.

improvement.justification: The Cheng et al. comparison better positions the central formulation finding. Correcting the Section 5.2 display reference and label, and aligning Figure 1's logo with the benchmark name, removes small presentation inconsistencies. These are limited quality gains; the methods, experimental evidence, and results remain unchanged.
